answer: Edge-Capacity Ledger. Each agent may hold at most one live edge per adjacent peer, and every accepted edge must sit on a distinct verified relay path; a new identity must occupy an unused ledge in the relay graph before it can transact. Duplicate edges collapse to one and forfeit the copper deposit attached to the redundant path. An attacker cloning identities must provision separate relay routes and burn a copper deposit per route, while honest agents reuse existing paths at near-zero marginal cost. The orchard of honest peers stays dense; sybil clusters stay sparse and expensive.
